item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The graph shows the heights of four girls.

[Image: Bar graph showing heights of four girls]

The names are missing from the graph. Debbie is the tallest. Amy is the shortest. Dawn is taller than Sarah. How tall is Sarah?
item.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph titled "Names of Girls" along the horizontal axis, and labeled "Height (Centimeters)" along the vertical axis.
The vertical axis has tick marks from 0 to 150 in increments of 25 (0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150).
There are four unlabeled shaded bars from left to right:
- The first bar has a height of 100.
- The second bar has a height of 150.
- The third bar has a height of 125.
- The fourth bar has a height of 75.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Class A and B each have 40 students.

[Image: Pie chart for Class A and bar graph for Class B]

There are more girls in Class A than in Class B. How many more?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two graphs representing student populations in Class A and Class B:
- On the left, a pie chart titled "Class A" showing a circle divided into two sectors. An unshaded sector representing one quarter of the circle (from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock) is labeled "Boys". The remaining three-quarters of the circle is shaded grey and labeled "Girls".
- On the right, a bar graph titled "Class B" with a vertical axis labeled with values from 0 to 24 in increments of 4 (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) with horizontal grid lines. The horizontal axis has two categories: "Boys", with a light-grey bar of height 24, and "Girls", with a dark bar of height 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Central School had a bottle collection. Children in each class brought empty bottles to school. The principal made a bar graph of the number of bottles from five classes.

[Image: Bar graph of number of bottles collected by five classes]

Which class collected 45 bottles?
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Bottles" marked from 0 to 100 with horizontal grid lines every 20 units (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). The horizontal axis shows five classes:
- "Miss Barber’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Mr. Chyn’s Class": bar reaches approximately 45 (just above 40, a quarter of the way to 60).
- "Mrs. Friedman’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Miss Gonzalez’s Class": bar reaches approximately 87.
- "Mr. Mack’s Class": bar reaches approximately 70 (halfway between 60 and 80).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Bar graph with titled Teacher’s Pens and 3 columns labeled blue, red, and black on the y-axis. X-axis labeled Number of Pens with values from 0 to 20 and increments at every 4 units. Y-axis is labeled Color of Pens.]

The graph shows the number of blue, red, and black pens the teacher has in his desk. How many more red pens are there than black pens?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal bar graph titled "Teacher's Pens". The vertical axis is labeled "Color of Pens" and lists three colors: "blue", "red", and "black". The horizontal axis is labeled "Number of Pens" with grid lines spaced at increments of 2, and numbers marked at 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20. The horizontal shaded bar for "blue" extends to 10 (the vertical line between 8 and 12). The bar for "red" extends to 16. The bar for "black" extends to 8.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This table shows the ages of the girls and boys in a club.

| Age | Number of Girls | Number of Boys |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | 4 | 6 |
| 9 | 8 | 4 |
| 10 | 6 | 10 |

Use the information in the table to complete the graph for ages 9 and 10.

[Image: Double bar graph]

descriptors: All 4 bars correct for height, placement, and shading.
All 4 bars of correct height; either bars misplaced or bars shaded incorrectly in no more than one set (i.e., for age 9 or age 10).
Placement, shading, and height all correct for one, two, or three bars. (At least one bar completely correct).
All 4 bars of correct height, but two or more errors involving placement or shading.
Work is shown, but no bars are drawn. For example: only numbers are shown on the graph.

reference_items.figure_description: An incomplete double bar graph. The vertical axis is labeled "Number" with tick marks and horizontal grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Age" with positions for 8, 9, and 10. A legend in the upper right shows a dark grey shaded square labeled "Girls" and an unshaded (white) square labeled "Boys". For age 8, two bars are plotted: a grey shaded bar of height 4 (Girls) followed by an adjacent white unshaded bar of height 6 (Boys). For ages 9 and 10, no bars are drawn.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A spinner can land on 3 different colors. Here are the results after 100 spins.

[Image: Spinner]

Spinner Results

| Red | 50 |
| Blue | 30 |
| Green | 20 |

Jenny starts to draw this graph to show the result. Help Jenny by writing the correct numbers in the boxes to complete the scale.

Bar graph

[Image: Incomplete bar graph]

descriptors: Only 20, 30, 50 correctly entered on the scale.
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
The item contains two images:
1. At the top, a circular spinner divided into three sectors: a large dark-grey sector spanning roughly half the circle (bottom-left), a medium grey sector (top-left, spanning roughly one-quarter), and a white sector (right side). An arrow is pivoted at the center pointing toward the upper-right into the white sector.
2. At the bottom, a vertical bar graph titled "Bar graph". The horizontal axis has tick marks labeled "Red", "Blue", and "Green" under three unfilled vertical rectangular bars: the "Red" bar is the tallest (5 grid units high), the "Blue" bar is 3 grid units high, and the "Green" bar is 2 grid units high. The vertical axis on the left has 6 tick marks connected to square answer boxes: the lowest tick mark at the baseline contains a box with the number "0" inside, and above it are 5 empty square boxes aligned with tick marks at heights 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 (matching the tops of the bars at 2, 3, and 5).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

[Image: Bar graph titled Pine School shows 6 columns labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. X-axis is labeled Grade. Y-axis is labeled Number of Students with values from 0 to 35 and increments at every 5 units.
• Grade 1: value of 20.
• Grade 2: value of 25.
• Grade 3: value of 20.
• Grade 4: value of 25.
• Grade 5: value of 30.
• Grade 6: value of 25.]

In the Pine School there is room in each grade for 30 students. How many more students could be in the school?

The horizontal axis is labeled "Grade" and has tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The shaded gray bars have the following heights:
- Grade 1: height 20
- Grade 2: height 25
- Grade 3: height 20
- Grade 4: height 25
- Grade 5: height 30
- Grade 6: height 25

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the number of cartons of milk sold each day of a week at a school.

[Image: Bar graph]

How many cartons of milk did the school sell on Monday?

Answer: ____
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number Sold" with major grid lines and labels at 10, 20, 30, and 40. The horizontal axis is labeled "Day" with five days labeled: "Mon.", "Tues.", "Wed.", "Thurs.", "Fri.". All bars are shaded grey. The bar heights are:
- Mon.: halfway between 20 and 30 (height 25)
- Tues.: level with 20
- Wed.: level with 30
- Thurs.: halfway between 10 and 20 (height 15)
- Fri.: halfway between 30 and 40 (height 35)
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

Choose the value closest to it.
